neighbours.label: the word ' effective' meaning that something works well for its purpose (an effective treatment, the most effective means), as opposed to synonyms like useful or strong in the same sentence
fire: Doctors say that regular walking is an effective way to lower blood pressure.
Mulch remains the most effective tool for keeping weeds out of a garden.
Her lawyers found an effective argument against the new parking rule.
Salt water is a surprisingly effective remedy for a mild sore throat.
Teachers want an effective method of teaching fractions to young children.
A sturdy fence is the most effective defense against hungry deer.
The study reports that this cream is an effective treatment for dry skin.
The city needs an effective plan to reduce traffic near the schools.
quiet: Doctors say that regular walking is a pleasant way to spend an evening.
Mulch remains the most popular product for keeping weeds out of a garden.
Her lawyers found a long argument against the new parking rule.
Salt water is a surprisingly common remedy for a mild sore throat.
Teachers want a new method of teaching fractions to young children.
A sturdy fence is the most expensive defense against hungry deer.
The study reports that this cream is a popular treatment for dry skin.
The city needs a cheap plan to reduce traffic near the schools.

short: ' effective': works well for its purpose
notes: Card: ' effective' x21, ' Effective' x3 of the top 32; the + pole predicts effective and fires before it. Probes: effective strategy 0.56, safe and effective 0.24, most effective and 0.82 on ' and', Effective leaders 0.41; useful strategy 0.02, efficient 0.06, ineffective 0.06, 'becomes effective on March 1' 0.12, efficacy 0.10, 'worked very well' 0.27 on ' very'.
